clue.text: Where patients need to be patient?

definitions.text: Where patients need to be patient?

parts.words: Where patients need to be patient?
parts.note: the place at a surgery where people sit before their appointment, with a play on patients needing patience

explanation.surface: A wry remark about the long waits at a doctor's surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun is on 'patients' (people seeing a doctor) and 'patient' (willing to wait): the room is where you wait your turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's surgery has a room where people sit until they are called in, which is where their patience is tested.

clue.text: A royal wandering?

parts.note: a monarch strolling among a crowd to meet people informally rather than roaming aimlessly

explanation.surface: A king or queen idly roaming about.
explanation.walkthrough: Royals famously go on informal strolls through crowds to greet the public; 'wandering' suggests aimless roaming but means that kind of meet-the-people tour.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names an informal stroll by a dignitary through a crowd, chatting with onlookers, a custom popularised by the British royal family.

clue.text: The moment for some coffee?

definitions.meaning: a very brief moment of time
a type of coffee made from soluble powder by adding hot water

explanation.surface: Someone decides now is the time for a cup of coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a split second of time; the other is soluble powdered coffee made quickly with hot water.

clue.text: Broke the rules in going over the border before break of day

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece going over another sits above it, so it comes first
this piece comes before the final letter in the answer

parts.note: taken as written
a fringe is an edge or border

indicators.note: the break of day is its very start, so the first letter of day

explanation.surface: Someone crossed a frontier illegally just before dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' and 'before' set the order in this down light; 'break of day' means dawn on the surface but here signals only the opening letter of 'day'.
explanation.definitionFit: To infringe is to break or violate a rule, so the past tense means broke the rules.

clue.text: Superficial brilliance of marginal explanation

definitions.meaning: a shine or lustre on the surface only
a note written in the margin of a text explaining a word

explanation.surface: A phrase that sounds like a sneer at a showy but shallow commentary.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a surface shine and an explanatory note added in a manuscript's margin.

clue.text: In which rowers might get in a tangle?

definitions.text: In which rowers might get in a tangle?

parts.words: In which rowers might get in a tangle?
parts.note: a seaweed where oars could become snagged, with tangle also being a name for a type of kelp

explanation.surface: A boat crew getting their oars all knotted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangle' looks like a mess of oars, but it is also an old name for a kind of large brown seaweed; this weed's name begins with the very thing rowers pull.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large brown seaweed, a kelp, which could snarl the blades of anyone rowing through it.

clue.text: Amah did include religious leader

indicators.note: the words amah did contain the answer's letters running across them

explanation.surface: An Asian nursemaid kept a cleric among her charges.
explanation.walkthrough: An amah is a nursemaid in parts of Asia; the letters run from inside 'Amah' into 'did'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islam, the title names a prophesied redeemer, and has been claimed by various Muslim leaders.

clue.text: Said school members coming from the country

indicators.note: said tells us the words are spoken, so a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: a school is a group of whales or other sea mammals, so its members are whales

explanation.surface: Pupils are said to come from a rural area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' suggests pupils, but it is a group of sea mammals; their name sounds like the country.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the four nations of the United Kingdom, west of England.

clue.text: Stream, a wet sort above right channel

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed above the next
to sort things is to rearrange them, so the letters of a wet are shuffled

parts.note: a course is the channel along which a river or stream flows

explanation.surface: A damp kind of fellow perched beside a stream-fed channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' signals the anagram of 'a wet'; in a down light 'above' means the shuffled letters come first. 'Stream' and 'channel' both look like definitions; the second is the course a river follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A watercourse is a brook, river or other flowing body of water, or the bed it runs in.

clue.text: Performance at nightclub that had not been staged?

definitions.text: Performance at nightclub that had not been staged?

parts.words: Performance at nightclub that had not been staged?
parts.note: entertainment given on the dance area rather than on a raised platform, playing on staged as faked

explanation.surface: Suspicion that a nightclub act was improvised or a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not been staged' seems to mean genuine or unrehearsed, but literally the act was not put on a stage: it happened at ground level.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret entertainment at a nightclub is presented on the dance area among the tables rather than on a raised platform.

clue.text: Like two similar springs?

parts.note: two water sources alike to each other, read as a pair suited to one another

explanation.surface: A remark on a pair of identical coiled springs.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'spring' can be a water source, which is also called a well, so two alike springs are wells that pair up neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means suitably paired or evenly balanced, and here also suggests two wells that are equal.

clue.text: Martha laminated part of the flowers' receptacles

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman sealed some floral specimens in plastic.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany the receptacle, the part of the stalk bearing a flower's organs, is also called by this Greek-derived term in the plural.

clue.text: Extra particular

definitions.meaning: something additional or out of the ordinary
specific to one person or thing

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both additional or exceptional and specific to one case.

clue.text: Marsupial finds way to resting-place

parts.note: roo is a short form of kangaroo, a pouched mammal
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A kangaroo discovers the path to somewhere it can sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch where birds settle to sleep is a place of rest.

clue.text: The whole bag of tricks

parts.note: in bridge, winning every trick in a deal, read through the idiom for everything available

explanation.surface: An idiom meaning everything one has at one's disposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bag' suggests the idiom, but in bridge a player bags tricks; taking all thirteen in one deal is the top achievement. It also means winning all of a sport's major titles in a year.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, the term means taking all thirteen tricks in a hand.

clue.text: A lady on the shelf turned up bloomer

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: Mary is a woman's name

indicators.note: in a down light, turned up means the word for a shelf is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a sill is a shelf at the foot of a window

explanation.surface: A woman left unmarried later found herself an object of interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the shelf' suggests a spinster, but it is a window ledge; 'turned up' reverses SILL to LLIS, placed under A MARY by 'on'. 'bloomer' is a flower, not a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer here is something that blooms: this is a lily-like plant grown for its showy trumpet flowers.

clue.text: Grease used until crab founders

indicators.note: a ship that founders sinks and breaks up, so the letters of until crab collapse into a new order

explanation.surface: A crab needs oiling until it sinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'founders' (sinks) rearranges the letters of UNTIL CRAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease is an oily substance used to reduce friction between moving parts, as are similar oils.

clue.text: Figures coming from hot arcade

indicators.note: the answer comes out of these letters by reshuffling the words hot arcade

explanation.surface: Numbers or shapes emerging from a warm shopping gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming from' asks for the letters of HOT ARCADE to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: These are solid geometric shapes, each with eight flat faces.

clue.text: He had bent coin pleasure-seeking

parts.note: contracted to he'd, written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: something bent is out of shape, so the letters of coin are twisted round

explanation.surface: A man had a buckled coin and loved a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' signals the anagram of 'coin'; 'He had' must be squeezed into its contracted written form, with the apostrophe dropped as grids ignore punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an adjective for anything relating to or devoted to the pursuit of enjoyment.

clue.text: Cut short part of old measure

indicators.note: cut short means the clue word loses its last letter

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: A truncated piece of an outdated unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' reads as a verb phrase in the surface, but 'short' tells the solver to drop the final letter of 'Cut' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: It was an ancient unit of length based on the forearm, about eighteen inches.

clue.text: One or two fish

parts.note: cod is a common sea fish
ling is a long slender fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A fishmonger offering either a single fish or a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue both defines and builds: the answer is a single fish (a young cod, or a kind of apple) and is also two fish joined.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a young cod, a single fish, and also splits into the names of two separate fish.

clue.text: Requisition but not for the first time

definitions.text: Requisition but not for the first time

parts.words: Requisition but not for the first time
parts.note: placing an order once more, a repeat request for goods

explanation.surface: An official demand for supplies, made a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To place another request for goods that were requested before is to order them again.

clue.text: Leaves in the desert

parts.note: patches of foliage found among the sands, playing on leaves as departs

explanation.surface: Someone abandons another in the wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb (abandons) but is plural foliage: the green fertile spots amid arid sand.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot in a desert, where water allows trees and greenery to grow.

clue.text: Have a royal time?

parts.note: to occupy the throne for a period, read against the idiom for enjoying oneself

explanation.surface: An invitation to enjoy oneself grandly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a royal time' suggests great fun, but it is literally a monarch's period of rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign's period on the throne; as a verb, to rule as monarch.

clue.text: I did shy away from language

indicators.note: away indicates the letters of i did shy are sent off in different directions and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they avoided talking in some tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' rearranges the letters of I DID SHY.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the vernacular of Ashkenazi Jews, a Germanic tongue written in Hebrew script.

clue.text: German city took item back with almost everything that's crucial

parts.note: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr

indicators.note: taken back means the short word for an item is read in reverse

parts.note: it is a thing or item

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for everything is dropped

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone from a German city returned a vital object with nearly all their belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses IT to TI; 'almost' drops the last letter of ALL to give AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indispensable or of vital importance is absolutely necessary.

clue.text: Merlin did not begin with goat

indicators.note: the word for Merlin loses its opening letter, so it does not start

parts.note: Merlin is the wizard of Arthurian legend

explanation.surface: The Arthurian sorcerer failed to start out with a nanny goat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did not begin' removes the first letter of WIZARD.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Pyrenean chamois, a goat-antelope of the mountains.

clue.text: Foreknowledge — is it why we need two eyes?

definitions.meaning: the supposed power to perceive future events

definitions.text: is it why we need two eyes?
definitions.meaning: humorously, a spare second pair of vision in reserve, as in a backup eye

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about why humans have a pair of eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the phrase literally: a second means of seeing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the gift of clairvoyance, and literally a backup ability to see.
